newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says to review ties if NATO ignores Russia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says to review ties if NATO ignores Russia.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, striving to overcome communist and nationalist criticism of his treaty deal with NATO, told parliamentary leaders on Monday he would review relations if the alliance ignored Russia's views.

"If NATO begins to take decisions without taking account of Russia's opinion, Russia will review its relations with the alliance," Interfax news agency quoted him as saying. Russian and NATO officials say the treaty, to be signed next week, gives Moscow a blocking vote on NATO decisions affecting Russia but not an outright veto on all the alliance's affairs.

Yeltsin told the speakers and party leaders from both houses of parliament that Russia had won important assurances from the West, including a pledge not to move nuclear weapons or other forces into new member states in eastern Europe.

The president, who acknowledged last week that Moscow was unable to prevent NATO admitting former Soviet-bloc states in eastern Europe, said the NATO-Russia Founding Act should be seen "not as a compromise but as a balanced result, corresponding to our interests and the interests of the alliance".

Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov, whose party is the biggest bloc in the State Duma lower house, said at the weekend that the treaty was "practically an act of capitulation". The treaty does not, however, require parliamentary ratification.

Yeltsin urged the deputies to speed up their ratification of the global chemical weapons ban treaty and the START-2 nuclear arms limitation pact. He also said differences with Belarus on plans for union would be settled before he and Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko signed a treaty on Friday.
